title: Backend Engineering & API Design
summary: Build production Java services and long-lived synchronous/asynchronous contracts rather than CRUD controllers.

modules.title: Spring Core & Spring Boot runtime
modules.summary: Understand inversion of control and Boot automation well enough to debug what the framework creates.
modules.why: Framework productivity is useful only when bean lifecycle, configuration and runtime wiring are not magic.

units.title: IoC container, beans & dependency injection
units.summary: Understand object creation, discovery and dependency wiring.
units.challenge: Build equivalent manual wiring and Spring wiring, then diagnose a circular dependency.
units.evidence: Dependency graph plus explanation of container responsibilities.

units.title: Configuration, profiles & auto-configuration
units.summary: Control environment-specific behaviour without hidden configuration surprises.
units.challenge: Create dev/test/prod configurations and inspect why a particular auto-configuration activates.
units.evidence: Configuration-precedence table and condition report.

units.title: Lifecycle, health & Actuator
units.summary: Expose operational state and participate correctly in deployment lifecycle.
units.challenge: Make a service reject traffic until dependencies are ready and drain safely on shutdown.
units.evidence: Deployment sequence with observed health-state transitions.

modules.title: Backend application structure & boundaries
modules.summary: Separate transport, application, domain and infrastructure responsibilities before distributing them across services.
modules.why: Most service maintainability problems begin as unclear in-process boundaries.

units.title: Transport, application & domain boundaries
units.summary: Keep HTTP/framework details from leaking into business rules.
units.challenge: Refactor a controller-heavy feature into clear boundaries.
units.evidence: Package/dependency diagram and tests proving domain independence from Spring.

units.title: Validation & error boundaries
units.summary: Validate at the right layer and translate failures deliberately.
units.challenge: Create validation at transport/domain/persistence boundaries without duplication.
units.evidence: Error taxonomy and representative API responses.

units.title: Application transaction boundaries
units.summary: Align transaction scope with business invariants rather than controller calls.
units.challenge: Fix a workflow that holds DB locks while calling a slow external service.
units.evidence: Before/after sequence diagram showing shorter transaction scope.

modules.title: HTTP semantics for API engineers
modules.summary: Use HTTP methods, status, caching and conditional semantics correctly.
modules.why: A REST API is a protocol contract, not JSON over POST.

units.title: Methods, status codes & representation semantics
units.summary: Map operations to HTTP semantics precisely.
units.challenge: Review a deliberately poor CRUD API and correct method/status/header use.
units.evidence: API contract before/after with justification.

units.title: Conditional requests & HTTP caching
units.summary: Use validators and cache controls for performance and concurrency.
units.challenge: Add optimistic concurrency and cache validation to a resource endpoint.
units.evidence: Concurrent-edit and cache-validation tests.

units.title: Streaming, ranges & large HTTP payloads
units.summary: Avoid buffering everything into memory and support efficient transfers.
units.challenge: Implement a large export/download without loading the entire file into heap.
units.evidence: Memory profile and client behaviour under cancellation.

modules.title: REST resource & workflow design
modules.summary: Design stable resources, commands and long-running workflows from product semantics.
modules.why: Good resource modeling reduces special-case endpoints and compatibility pain.

units.title: Resource modeling & URI design
units.summary: Expose domain concepts without mirroring database tables mechanically.
units.challenge: Design APIs for projects, memberships, tasks and transitions with three alternative models.
units.evidence: Resource model and trade-off note.

units.title: Pagination, filtering, sorting & sparse retrieval
units.summary: Keep collection APIs stable and scalable as data grows.
units.challenge: Implement offset and keyset pagination, then demonstrate consistency/performance differences.
units.evidence: Query plans and duplicate/missing-item scenarios.

units.title: Bulk & long-running operations
units.summary: Represent work that cannot finish inside one request reliably.
units.challenge: Design import/export and bulk-update operations with resume/cancel/error reporting.
units.evidence: State machine and API specification.

modules.title: API correctness: idempotency, concurrency & retries
modules.summary: Make externally visible side effects safe under duplicate requests and uncertain networks.
modules.why: Clients retry when outcomes are unknown; APIs must make duplicate intent explicit.

units.title: Idempotency keys & request deduplication
units.summary: Protect non-idempotent operations from duplicate side effects.
units.challenge: Implement idempotent create/payment-like endpoint and crash between side effect and response.
units.evidence: Failure tests proving one logical side effect under retries.

units.title: Optimistic concurrency at API boundaries
units.summary: Prevent lost updates without globally serializing users.
units.challenge: Reproduce lost update from two clients and fix with conditional writes.
units.evidence: Concurrent-client test and conflict response design.

units.title: Retryable API contracts
units.summary: Tell clients what can be retried and how backoff/rate limits interact.
units.challenge: Define a client/server retry policy for transient dependency failures and overload.
units.evidence: Retry matrix with unsafe combinations called out.

modules.title: API versioning, compatibility & governance
modules.summary: Evolve contracts without breaking independent clients and teams.
modules.why: The cost of an API is dominated by change after consumers exist.

units.title: OpenAPI & contract-first design
units.summary: Make API shape machine-readable and reviewable.
units.challenge: Write an OpenAPI contract before implementing one feature and generate a client stub.
units.evidence: Reviewed spec plus implementation conformance tests.

units.title: Backward compatibility & versioning strategies
units.summary: Prefer additive evolution and explicit compatibility windows.
units.challenge: Evolve an API through five changes and classify compatibility impact.
units.evidence: Compatibility table and rollout plan.

units.title: Deprecation, ownership & API governance
units.summary: Scale contract quality across many teams without central bottlenecks.
units.challenge: Design governance for 50 teams publishing APIs.
units.evidence: Lifecycle policy including metrics and exception path.

modules.title: GraphQL API architecture
modules.summary: Use GraphQL when flexible graph-shaped querying justifies server/runtime complexity.
modules.why: GraphQL solves specific client/data composition problems but moves cost control and caching concerns server-side.

units.title: Schema, types & resolvers
units.summary: Model a graph API and its execution boundaries.
units.challenge: Model project/task/member data as GraphQL schema and implement resolvers.
units.evidence: Schema plus query examples and error/nullability rationale.

units.title: N+1, batching & query cost
units.summary: Protect backend systems from flexible query amplification.
units.challenge: Reproduce N+1 queries and implement batching plus depth/cost protection.
units.evidence: DB-query count and latency before/after.

units.title: GraphQL caching, security & evolution
units.summary: Operate GraphQL with authorization and compatibility at field level.
units.challenge: Design GraphQL for multi-team ownership with per-field authorization and deprecation.
units.evidence: Architecture memo comparing GraphQL to REST/BFF for the product.

modules.title: gRPC & Protocol Buffers
modules.summary: Design efficient typed service-to-service contracts and streaming RPCs.
modules.why: Internal low-latency communication has different constraints from public web APIs.

units.title: Protobuf schema & evolution
units.summary: Design binary contracts that remain compatible across deployments.
units.challenge: Evolve a message through several versions without breaking old clients.
units.evidence: Compatibility test matrix.

units.title: Unary & streaming RPC
units.summary: Choose request/streaming modes and propagate deadlines/cancellation.
units.challenge: Implement a streaming activity feed and handle client cancellation.
units.evidence: Sequence diagram and deadline/cancellation tests.

units.title: gRPC load balancing, retries & observability
units.summary: Operate RPCs across dynamic service fleets.
units.challenge: Design gRPC communication across multiple service instances with failure handling.
units.evidence: Operational architecture and retry safety analysis.

modules.title: Webhooks, SSE & WebSockets
modules.summary: Choose server-to-client/event callbacks based on directionality, delivery and connection needs.
modules.why: Polling is not the only choice, and persistent connections introduce lifecycle/scale costs.

units.title: Reliable webhook design
units.summary: Deliver server-to-server callbacks despite retries, duplicates and consumer downtime.
units.challenge: Build webhook delivery with signing, retry and manual replay.
units.evidence: Failure tests covering duplicate/out-of-order/unavailable receiver.

units.title: Server-Sent Events
units.summary: Use one-way streaming over HTTP for incremental updates.
units.challenge: Stream long-running job progress and reconnect without losing position.
units.evidence: Reconnect demo and infrastructure caveat list.

units.title: WebSocket connection lifecycle
units.summary: Manage bidirectional persistent connections, heartbeats and reconnection.
units.challenge: Build real-time comments and survive server restart/reconnect.
units.evidence: Connection state machine and resilience tests.

modules.title: Background jobs & scheduling
modules.summary: Run work outside request latency while preserving correctness, retries and ownership.
modules.why: Many production workflows are naturally asynchronous and cannot be trusted to one request thread.

units.title: Job state, retries & idempotency
units.summary: Represent asynchronous work as explicit durable state.
units.challenge: Build a durable export job that can crash/restart safely.
units.evidence: Job state machine and crash-recovery tests.

units.title: Cron, scheduled work & time semantics
units.summary: Handle recurring execution, missed runs and timezone/calendar concerns.
units.challenge: Design a tenant-local daily digest across timezones and DST changes.
units.evidence: Schedule test matrix and overlap policy.

units.title: Distributed scheduler architecture
units.summary: Coordinate many workers without executing the same logical job incorrectly.
units.challenge: Design a scheduler for millions of delayed jobs.
units.evidence: Architecture with partitioning, failover and duplicate-execution handling.

modules.title: BFF, API gateways & service composition
modules.summary: Place aggregation, policy and protocol translation at deliberate boundaries.
modules.why: Gateway layers can simplify clients or become high-coupling bottlenecks.

units.title: Backend-for-Frontend pattern
units.summary: Shape backend aggregation around a specific client experience when justified.
units.challenge: Design one shared API and two BFF alternatives for web/mobile clients.
units.evidence: Decision memo identifying where BFF reduces or increases coupling.

units.title: API gateway responsibilities
units.summary: Separate cross-cutting edge policy from business orchestration.
units.challenge: Define what belongs and does not belong in a gateway for a multi-service product.
units.evidence: Responsibility matrix and failure-domain analysis.

units.title: Request aggregation & composition failures
units.summary: Avoid turning frontend convenience into a distributed transaction of read calls.
units.challenge: Optimize an aggregator calling six downstream services under partial failure.
units.evidence: Latency budget and degradation policy.
